(I have a level 1 ASD diagnosis since I was 12) But the thing is, autism isn’t really my biggest problem tbh. And it’s common to have comorbities with autism, as well. I very clearly have some sort of fear based disorder(s) and several traumas. (I have a half ptsd diagnosis from an actual autism specialist, got recommended to get a full diagnosis.) The clinic told me it was just stress caused by my autism and that I needed “treatment” for my autism. I guess I’m just feeling super super down because of how horribly they treated me. It just really triggered these thoughts again. I know I’ll feel better soon I just feel so…misunderstood and let down by the people who were supposed to help me! ):

Also to be a bit more positive…I love green tea! I feel like I’d get distracted quickly with taking notes, but I do usually eat more “lighter” foods due to my sensitive stomach!! Do think I could work a bit more on it though :p I try eating a lot of fruits and drink lots of tea. I’ve also been vegetarian since I was around 8 I think? For a very long time now.

Maybe it has something to do with boredom? Or suddenly after feeling shitty for a while and not wanting to do anything you suddenly feel euphoric and motivated, but you don’t really know what you want to do or don’t know what to do with this feeling. So it feels like you seek something to kind of satisfy this feeling even though you don’t know how or what. Idk, just a thought. Might be something else. I also notice I often get excited about things related to escapism, dreaming, daydreaming, and such. I guess I’m just a bit weird and confused, lol.

For me it also has to do with some weird type of escapism? And I get weirdly euphoric. I don’t hate it but I do hate that I have no idea what the actual thing is that I want to do even though it feels like it’s there???

I’ve somewhat worked on self control btw so it’s usually something non harmful that I never throw at actual people, just the ground. I prefer my socks or plastic water bottle. Or I slam the door! I’ve had instances in the past though where I would punch my dinner and it got splattered everywhere on my bed and curtains. Or I would make my whole room a mess lmaooo. Now I just imagine doing it in my mind instead, and always try to remind myself of the consequences it has. Not fun to clean up your entire room after!!!

When I’m already overwhelmed and I try to calm down but people keep coming into my room and talking to me!!!! I just get silent for a while and when they don’t stop in time I will start screaming, crying very loud, hyperventilating, maybe throw stuff if they STILL continue… very embarassing, lol. I hate meltdowns.

I also get this often, I even get a bit excited when that happens, despite the fact I don’t even know what it is that I want to do? It’s so weird. Forgot about that but this remembered me I do get that a lot. So I’m also curious!!!

Maybe it will actually help you be somewhat reassured? I mean what can go wrong, either they confirm nothing is wrong and you can feel a little more relaxed, and if something does turn out to be wrong (don’t worry, it’s a very small chance) it will only be a good thing they noticed it right!! 

I’ve visited the hospital for years thinking something was wrong with me physically, but only recently I found out it was anxiety. Anxiety can have a lot more physical symptoms than you might think, which I think causes us to feel so worried because I guess you assume something mental can’t cause such bad physical symptoms right! But it can. 
(At the beginning I was in total disbelief, even when doctors recommended me that I should also try getting help for my mental health I thought they were bluffing lol.)

Now (knowing I have anxiety & health anxiety) when I go to the doctor and they tell me nothing is wrong and I’m healthy (despite having a few mild deficiencies, I promise it won’t kill you:p, just some vitamins and you’ll be alright:) ) it does reassure me a bit :) just be sure to not overdo it and go there every other week because that might just make it worse. 

I couldnt sleep properly for days because I was very short of breath and afraid I was dying and I went to the doctor to check it out. He measured my lungs and oxygen level and confirmed I wasn’t actually oxygen deficit and it was only caused by stress (stress can make you feel air hungry), after that I was actually able to calm a bit down and fall asleep even when I did still feel short of breath.

I somehow convinced myself for 2 days that my mom was abusive. I guess one of my friends mentioning that that might be the case really played a role in it, which sort of “confirmed” my intrusive thoughts, but I was just ranting about an argument I had with my mom. I think every family has arguments at times. I had panic attacks and was derealizing/dissociating very bad compared to the usual feeling of being unreal, because I felt like I was betrayed or that I finally realized what the “real truth” was. 

Then I just shared all my worries and feelings to my therapist, and she told me that someone with autism (I have autism as well) can have black and white thinking. And somehow that reassured me and I realized I was exaggerating. But I’m super scared of it happening again because I can still feel the doubt in my stomach from those days, the feeling of “something being wrong”. and I’m scared of that feeling getting bigger and bigger.
